analysis.title: Equity Reverse Convertible Model Portfolios
key_insights: UBS CIO publishes USD, EUR and CHF reverse convertible (RC) model portfolios of ten equally weighted stocks each, focused on six-month tenors, built with the CIO RC methodology.
Single-stock implied volatility continues to command a healthy premium over index volatility, which supports RC coupons.

The CIO methodology combines market data (implied volatility, momentum) with fundamentals (leverage, valuation ratios). It favors stocks with relatively high implied volatility but lower risk metrics than peers.

Eligibility requires a stock to be 'CIO Selected' or rated Buy by UBS Investment Bank. For CHF stocks, Neutral-rated names also qualify because the universe is smaller. Sector exposure is capped at 30% per portfolio.
Low-implied-volatility stocks are excluded because they cannot deliver a coupon above a minimum threshold.
Figure 1 shows a higher CIO score is associated with higher put-writing returns. It is based on annualized average returns for 3-, 6- and 12-month tenors, solving for a 10% p.a. option premium.

UBS says the CIO methodology has performed well over the past 10 years and better than benchmark approaches such as picking the highest-implied-volatility stocks. It adds that past performance is no guarantee of future returns.
Worst-of baskets are presented as a way to raise yield in low-yielding base currencies (CHF, EUR) or in defensive, low-volatility sectors where single underlyings yield too little.

Basket construction has three steps: exclude the bottom 25-40% of stocks by score, form baskets of three (minimum two) top-scoring stocks in the same business area, then rank baskets by overall score. Basket pricing includes a 2% p.a. distribution fee.

An RC is a coupon-paying bond plus a short put on the underlying. If the underlying is at or above the strike at maturity, the investor gets the invested capital back. Below the strike, the investor receives the shares or their cash value.
Stated risks are loss of invested capital, limited secondary-market liquidity, issuer default risk, and returns capped at the coupon with no dividends or upside above the strike.
As of 1 November 2026, UBS CIO no longer rates or ranks equities in the Most Preferred, Bellwether and Least Preferred framework. It uses a 'CIO Selected' designation instead, which is not a rating.

trade_ideas.description: Six-month reverse convertible (short put plus bond) model portfolios in USD, EUR and CHF, ten equally weighted stocks each, sector cap 30%
trade_ideas.rationale: Generate income from the single-stock implied volatility premium while waiting to buy the stock at a lower level.
trade_ideas.risk: Loss of invested capital if the stock ends below the strike, issuer default risk, limited liquidity, and returns capped at the coupon.

trade_ideas.description: CIO worst-of baskets of three (minimum two) top-scoring same-sector stocks, with the three best-scoring baskets starred
trade_ideas.rationale: Worst-of baskets raise yield in low-yielding base currencies such as CHF and EUR or in defensive, low-volatility sectors.
trade_ideas.risk: Exposure to the worst performer in the basket, with the same capital loss and issuer risks as a standard RC.

risk_factors: Loss of invested capital if the underlying falls significantly below the strike at expiry.
Limited secondary-market liquidity, so investors should be prepared to hold to maturity.
Returns are limited to the coupon, with no dividends or upside above the strike.
Demand and supply for protection (volatility) can change over time and affect return characteristics.
Structured investments carry embedded costs and fees, and their tax treatment may be complex.

The page 4 table notes define percentile as current 6-month at-the-money implied volatility against its past one-year range. Richness is current implied volatility minus realized volatility over the past year.
